summary: Frontend-only verification of the 2MB image upload removal / client-side downscale fix. Test 1 (profile-photo-upload in Profile Editor) PASSED with a synthetic 7.5MB JPEG: no 'Image size must be less than 2MB' alert, no console/runtime errors, preview image (data:image/jpeg base64 data URL) was set on profileForm.design_artist_photo. Regression with a small JPEG also passed silently. Test 2 (handleArtistPhotoUpload / #artist-photo-upload under activeTab==='design') could not be exercised via the live UI because the 'Design' tab is not present in the main navigation tabs list (see App.js line 5320 / 5397 - tabs array = ['onstage','songs','requests','analytics','profile','events',...]). The activeTab==='design' render block (App.js ~line 10785) is orphaned in the current nav. However, code review confirms handleArtistPhotoUpload (line 3724) is functionally identical to handleProfilePhotoUpload (both call the shared resizeImageForUpload helper, both have zero size checks) so behavior for >2MB uploads is expected to match Test 1 once the Design tab is reachable.

design_issues.screen: Design tab (Audience Page Design) - Artist Photo section
issues: Hint text still reads 'Max 2MB, JPG/PNG' (App.js ~line 10874) even though the 2MB client-side limit has been removed and images are now auto-downscaled. Consider updating copy to reflect the new behavior (e.g., 'Any size - photo will be resized automatically').

Design tab itself is not exposed in the primary navigation (tabs array in App.js lines 5320 & 5397 no longer includes 'design'), so end users cannot reach #artist-photo-upload from the UI. If this is intentional, dead code (10784-10979) can be removed; if unintentional, add 'design' back to the tabs list.

action_items: Update 'Max 2MB, JPG/PNG' hint under Artist Photo (App.js ~line 10874-10875) since the 2MB limit no longer applies.

Decide whether the Design tab (activeTab==='design') should be re-added to the tabs array or removed entirely; today users can't reach #artist-photo-upload / handleArtistPhotoUpload through the live UI.
critical_code_review_comments: resizeImageForUpload correctly handles EXIF orientation via createImageBitmap({imageOrientation:'from-image'}) and gracefully falls back to Image+FileReader on older browsers - good defensive coding.
Both handlers now share the helper and cleanly reject only for non-image files with a friendly alert - no more 2MB rejection.

handleProfilePhotoUpload alerts on error only (silent success), while handleArtistPhotoUpload alerts on success ('Photo uploaded successfully!'). Slight UX inconsistency but matches the requested spec.
App.js is 16,382 lines - well beyond the >700 line guideline. Recommend refactoring into feature modules (profile editor, design settings, etc.) in a follow-up.

success_rate.frontend: Profile photo flow: 100%. Artist photo flow: code path verified but live UI not reachable.

seed_data_creation: Generated /tmp/big.jpg (~7.5MB JPEG, 3000x3000) and /tmp/small.jpg (1.3KB) for upload tests. Not persisted server-side.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Profile photo upload fix verified end-to-end with a 7.5MB JPEG. Artist photo handler shares the same resizeImageForUpload helper so behavior is expected to be identical, but the Design tab is currently not reachable from the main nav (tabs list in App.js does not include 'design'). If main agent re-exposes the Design tab, run set_input_files('/tmp/big.jpg') against #artist-photo-upload and expect the 'Photo uploaded successfully! Click Save Changes to apply.' alert with no 2MB error.
rca of the issue: N/A - this run validated a fix, not investigated a bug. The prior 2MB rejection was removed from both handlers; downscaling now happens client-side via canvas.toDataURL('image/jpeg', 0.85) at max long edge 1600px, so a 7.5MB source becomes a much smaller base64 data URL suitable for storage.
